concepts.name: kudos
concepts.definition: The unit of recognition a giver gives a recipient. The word is the same in the singular and the plural: 1 kudos, 3 kudos. Not a point, credit or currency, and not a taco: :taco: is only the fallback default kudos emoji, used when the deployment sets none.

rejected.because: Michael chose the safe set of rejected names in grilling #8

concepts.name: member
concepts.definition: An active human in a workspace where Kudos is installed, guests included. Only members give and receive kudos; bots, deactivated people and people from another workspace are not members.

concepts.name: giver
concepts.definition: The member who gives kudos, by writing a kudos message or by chiming in on one, and spends their own daily allowance, then weekly reserve, on it.

concepts.name: recipient
concepts.definition: A member mentioned in a kudos message who receives its kudos. Every recipient receives one kudos for each kudos emoji in the message.

concepts.name: daily allowance
concepts.definition: How many kudos a giver can still give today from the workspace's base, minus what they have given today, and never below zero. It starts fresh at midnight in the giver's time zone, and nothing carries over. Bonus capacity from perks is the weekly reserve, spent only after the daily allowance is used up.

concepts.name: kudos emoji
concepts.definition: An emoji that gives kudos for a giver: the workspace's emoji, which is the deployment's default unless the workspace changes it (:taco: when the deployment sets none), plus the emoji in the giver's loadout while the store is visible to them. Each occurrence in a kudos message is one kudos for every recipient.

concepts.name: kudos message
concepts.definition: A message by a member with at least one kudos emoji and at least one mention. Only the message's own text counts, not code, quotes, strikethrough or attachments. It costs the giver one kudos per recipient per kudos emoji. Its words are kept as the kudos text while its newest revision is a kudos message.

concepts.name: attempt
concepts.definition: The evaluation of one kudos message against the rules and the giver's daily allowance. It ends in an outcome, and a retry evaluates it again. A message has at most one attempt and gives kudos at most once.

concepts.name: outcome
concepts.definition: How an attempt ended: Given (its recipients received kudos), Over allowance (it cost more than the daily allowance and weekly reserve left, so nothing was given) or Invalid (no mention could receive kudos).

concepts.name: award
concepts.definition: The kudos one giver gave one recipient through one kudos message or one chime-in. An award is permanent: neither editing nor deleting the message, nor removing a reaction, changes it (ADR-0001). Not a grant or gift.

rejected.because: Michael chose the safe set of rejected names in grilling #8

concepts.name: retry
concepts.definition: An edit to a message that has not given kudos which changes its mentions or kudos emoji, so it is evaluated again as if it were new. A retry that gives kudos spends the daily allowance of the day of the edit, then the weekly reserve; removing every kudos emoji instead withdraws the attempt.

concepts.name: skipped mention
concepts.definition: A mention in a kudos message that cannot receive kudos: the giver, a bot, a group or broadcast, or someone who is not a member. The other recipients still receive.

concepts.name: xp
concepts.definition: Experience a member earns: base XP on Given awards, 10 for each kudos given and 5 for each kudos received, bonus XP from perks the member owns, and personal quest and Journey rewards (P2). XP decides the member's level and never goes down (ADR-0002). It is not kudos and not coins.

concepts.name: level
concepts.definition: A member's rank in progression, from 1 upward with no cap, reached through XP: level 2 at 20 XP, level 3 at 100 XP, and from level L the next level needs 100 × (L − 1) more. Every level from level 5 gives one skill point, and levels 2 to 7 each unlock a feature.

concepts.name: skill point
concepts.definition: What each level from level 5 gives, spent on perks in the skill tree; levels 2 to 4 give none. Unspent skill points never expire, and a spent one is never refunded (ADR-0002). It is not kudos and not a coin.

concepts.name: perk
concepts.definition: Something a member owns for good from the perk list. An effect perk's first step costs skill points and its upgrade costs skill points and coins; an expression perk is bought with coins. Some need a minimum level. An active perk works only for a limited time after the member switches it on.

concepts.name: group aura
concepts.definition: The effect of a group perk: one member buys it, and every member who opted in and has the same primary group as its owner benefits. It follows its owner when they change primary group. Only the strongest aura of each kind counts, however many members own it.

concepts.name: booster
concepts.definition: A temporary effect that raises a member's bonus XP or chance of drops for a set time: an XP booster, a Discovery Lantern or a Crowd booster. Only one of each kind is active at a time.

concepts.name: weekly reserve
concepts.definition: Bonus kudos from perks for one week, spent only after the daily allowance is used up. It refills on Monday at midnight in the giver's time zone, and nothing carries over.

concepts.name: coin
concepts.definition: The currency a member earns from thoughtful giving and from being thanked by many different people, and spends in the store and on perk upgrades (ADR-0003). Coins never turn into kudos, and kudos never turn into coins.

concepts.name: store
concepts.definition: Where members spend coins on items they see before buying: kudos emoji now, and hedgehogs once they ship. Nothing in it is a random draw.

concepts.name: cosmetic
concepts.definition: A cut kind of unlock that only changed how kudos look, such as quips, cards and titles. What members own now are items. Every cosmetic had a rarity.

concepts.name: quip
concepts.definition: An unlocked flavour line the app posts under a kudos message when its giver uses one, so everyone in the channel can see it.

concepts.name: card
concepts.definition: An unlocked image the app shows with a quip, in a celebration or in the collection. A card is not a sticker: a sticker is a person in the sticker book.

concepts.name: title
concepts.definition: An unlocked name a member can show next to their own, such as Bridge Builder.

concepts.name: loadout
concepts.definition: A member's three kudos emoji slots, and their hedgehog once hedgehogs ship. The starter 🦔 fills the first slot until the member changes the loadout.

concepts.name: collection
concepts.definition: Every item a member owns: the starter, the items they bought and the items they earned.

concepts.name: rarity
concepts.definition: How rare a hoggie is: common, uncommon, rare, epic or legendary, each shown as a coloured square and its word (⬜ Common, 🟩 Uncommon, 🟦 Rare, 🟪 Epic, 🟧 Legendary) so it never reads by colour alone. Each rarity's weight is its chance per drop, versioned catalogue data, and a drop keeps the rarity it was drawn with. Rarity says nothing about the recognition behind it.

concepts.name: drop
concepts.definition: One hoggie a crate held, drawn by rarity at the crate's first successful open by its member and stored once, never changed: a pure function of the deployment's secret, the member, the crate and the catalogue version, so a repeated or retried open answers the same and nothing knows it before the open. Every crate a member opens themselves while collection is on drops one; duplicates count up.

concepts.name: unlock
concepts.definition: A feature of the game that a level makes ready for a member: quests at 2, the leaderboard at 3, the Book at 4, the skill tree at 5, coins and the inventory at 6, hedgehogs at 7. The member opens a ready unlock with one action, and it stays open for good. Unlocks gate what a member sees, never what they earn (ADR-0006).

concepts.name: achievement
concepts.definition: One tier of a ladder, earned once by doing something, such as thanking ten different people. It gives an exclusive cosmetic, never XP, skill points or coins, and it is never taken back.

rejected.because: use achievement or tier, never badge

concepts.name: ladder
concepts.definition: A series of four achievements for the same kind of action, each harder than the one before.

concepts.name: tier
concepts.definition: An achievement's place on its ladder: bronze, silver, gold or diamond. A tier is not a rarity.

concepts.name: streak
concepts.definition: A run of a member's workdays on which they gave at least one kudos. Days off and paused days neither add to it nor break it.

concepts.name: workday
concepts.definition: A day of the week a member works, Monday to Friday unless they change it. Only workdays count for streaks.

concepts.name: pause
concepts.definition: A future date a member marks as away, such as a holiday. It never breaks a streak and costs nothing.

concepts.name: freeze
concepts.definition: A store item that covers one missed workday so a streak survives, at most two missed workdays in a row. It adds no day to the streak.

concepts.name: thoughtful kudos
concepts.definition: A kudos message that says why its recipients earned it: for now, at least five words besides the mentions and kudos emoji. Only thoughtful kudos trigger bonus XP, perk effects, drops and coins, and spend the weekly reserve; every Given award still earns base XP.

concepts.name: chime-in
concepts.definition: A member's click on the app's kudos reaction under a given kudos message within a day of it, once per member and message; the message's giver and recipients cannot chime in. It gives each recipient one more kudos from the clicker's daily allowance, then weekly reserve, is thoughtful when the message was, and counts toward the message's chime-in thresholds.

rejected.because: the owner's later-feature name became the chime-in

concepts.name: chime-in threshold
concepts.definition: A number of chime-ins on one kudos message (3, 5, 10, 20, 50 or 100). Reaching one gives everyone who chimed in, and the giver, a stronger Crowd booster, and gives the recipients bonus XP.

concepts.name: sticker book
concepts.definition: A member's private album of the people they have thanked and the people who have thanked them, one sticker each, with an album for every group to complete: an album is complete once the member has thanked or been thanked by every other current member of the group, and it stays complete.

concepts.name: sticker
concepts.definition: A person in a member's sticker book. A sticker is not a cosmetic image, which is a card.

concepts.name: announcement channel
concepts.definition: A public channel a workspace admin picks for level-up and achievement notices: the only place HedgeHug celebrates progress in public, at its top level, and while none is picked nothing is celebrated in public (QM1, QM2).

concepts.name: xp booster
concepts.definition: A store item that, once switched on, adds a quarter to the base XP of the kudos a member gives for seven days. It never boosts received XP, and it adds to perk bonuses without compounding.

concepts.name: discovery lantern
concepts.definition: A store item that, once switched on, raises a member's chance of drops by a quarter for seven days. It never gives extra draws.

concepts.name: crowd booster
concepts.definition: A booster for 24 hours that a chime-in threshold gives everyone who chimed in on a kudos message and its giver, stronger at each higher threshold. Only the strongest Crowd booster a member holds counts.

concepts.name: group
concepts.definition: A Slack user group that counts for Kudos: every enabled custom user group unless a workspace admin picked an allowlist, never Slack's automatic admin and owner groups. A member can be in several groups. A group mention in a kudos message is still a skipped mention.

concepts.name: primary group
concepts.definition: The one group a member counts for on the group boards: one of the groups they are in, or none while they are in none. A member without one who joins groups gets the smallest of them by members, then name, then Slack ID, and keeps it until they leave it, it stops counting, or they pick another in the welcome message or Settings; losing it falls back to the smallest group left, or none, without a DM. Every change is kept, insert-only, in a history with its instant and cause (default, picked or fallback), so each kudos message counts for the giver's primary group at the moment it was given and switching never moves past kudos.

concepts.name: leaderboard
concepts.definition: A positive ranking of kudos given in a period (this week, this month or all time, by the giver's allowance day): groups by kudos given per member, then participation; and members inside their primary group or across the workspace, showing the top 3 and the member with the 3 people above and below. It never ranks kudos received or XP, and a member can leave the individual boards.

concepts.name: participation
concepts.definition: The share of a group's members who gave at least one kudos in a period. It breaks ties between groups on the leaderboard.

concepts.name: welcome message
concepts.definition: The one DM the app sends a member the first time they give or receive a Given award, in two versions: a first recipient's, headed by who thanked them, and a first giver's, headed by whom their first kudos landed with, with a neutral header for a welcome queued without either. Both say what HedgeHug is, what XP and the unlocks shown to the member bring, one next step toward giving three kudos, the daily allowance and, while the website opens to them, why to visit it; once groups exist, the pick of their primary group.

concepts.name: profile card
concepts.definition: What any member sees of another member: name, hedgehog avatar, primary group, level and achievement tiers. Never coins, perks, XP or kudos received.

concepts.name: sandbox
concepts.definition: The Slack workspace and its own Convex deployment where a new Kudos app is installed and proven before the real install. It runs a separate Slack app from the same manifest, with its own bot token and signing secret.

concepts.name: directory
concepts.definition: The app's record of a workspace's people: whether each is a member, a bot or not a member, and their time zone, and for a member the profile Slack gives (their email, real name, display name, title and picture) and whether they are a workspace admin or owner, and the workspace's user groups with the people in each. Slack keeps it fresh, eligibility and the allowance day are read from it when a kudos message is evaluated, a person it doesn't know makes the message wait, and a member who leaves keeps no profile.

concepts.name: indicator
concepts.definition: The one reaction the app shows on a kudos message for its outcome: the first kudos emoji the giver used for Given, an hourglass for Over allowance, a red X for Invalid, and none otherwise. It is desired state, so every delivery leaves the message showing the latest one.

concepts.name: domain event
concepts.definition: A fact a module publishes when something happened in the domain, such as kudosGiven, so that later modules react to it without the publisher knowing them. It is published in the transaction that made it true, and its shape only grows by adding fields.

concepts.name: hook
concepts.definition: A named point where a later module contributes to a decision another module makes without that module knowing it, such as the parse hooks of the kudos parser and, with the weekly reserve, the perks hook. Not the agent-host hooks that deliver Coherence.

concepts.name: parse hook
concepts.definition: A hook into the kudos parser: it names extra kudos emoji for a giver, or adds annotations about a message while its text is in memory. The workspace emoji hook names the workspace's kudos emoji; the thoughtful kudos hook adds the gate decision.

concepts.name: annotation
concepts.definition: A fact about a kudos message that a parse hook adds while the text is in memory, such as whether it says why, carried on kudosGiven in place of the text, which never leaves the kudos text.

concepts.name: revision
concepts.definition: One version of a chat message as the app saw it: the post, then each edit. Revisions are ordered (in Slack, by the edit's time, else the message's own), and a revision at or below the newest the app has seen for that message is ignored, so an original that arrives after its edit or a late older edit changes nothing (R21). A kudos message keeps only its newest revision, never its text.

concepts.name: app home
concepts.definition: A member's private page of Kudos in Slack, the app's Home tab. It shows how to give kudos, the daily allowance left today and when it refills, and the kudos the member gave and received this week and in total; later specs add their sections. For a member with a Home link it is the front door, a summary that sends them to the website for the rest (SW19).

concepts.name: HedgeHug
concepts.definition: The product's name as members see it: the Slack app, the bot, the slash command and the website. Code, classes and docs keep calling the product Kudos. Hug is flavour only, never the unit: the unit stays kudos.

concepts.name: website
concepts.definition: The signed-in browser surface where a member sees and manages their Kudos. It sits beside App Home and never replaces it.

concepts.name: effects record
concepts.definition: What progression writes once for one side of one award, the giver's or the recipient's: the base XP with the gate decision and the catalogue version in force, and in later stopping points the bonus XP, coins and drops. Effects records are insert-only and never recomputed (ADR-0004); a member's XP, level and skill points are derived from them.

concepts.name: gate decision
concepts.definition: Whether a kudos message is thoughtful kudos, decided once per revision by the thoughtful kudos parse hook from the text in memory and stored as an annotation: the rule version, thoughtful or not, and the word count. A recheck reuses it, a retry decides again, and every effects record copies the version and the verdict (P12).

concepts.name: levelReached
concepts.definition: The domain event progression publishes when a kudosGiven brings a member to a higher level: one per member and event, naming the highest level reached and the skill points it gave, with the kudos message that caused it (P6). Level-up DMs and public notices react to it.

concepts.name: level-up DM
concepts.definition: The direct message feedback sends a member, and only them, for each levelReached: the level reached, their saved skill points and the XP to the next level (P63, copy table). It is a notification, delivered by the Slack adapter at most 3 times, and not sent when the member's message setting for level ups is none.

concepts.name: public reply
concepts.definition: The one public message at the top level of the announcement channel that celebrates the progress members reached through a kudos message; posted once, then edited in place as sections from many modules (level notices, achievements) arrive, never under or beside the kudos message, and not at all while no announcement channel is picked. It states only progress, never the kudos text or the giver (P64, D18, QM1).

concepts.name: command
concepts.definition: A member's request from a chat surface, such as a click in App Home, that the adapter turns into a platform-neutral instruction (showHomeTab, showLeaderboard, setLeaderboardVisibility, setProgressSettings, setAnnouncementChannel) and the one command registry routes to the module that owns its state, behind that command's own flag. A command carries the value it sets, so repeating one changes nothing. Not a slash command: /hedgehug is Slack's typed command, which the adapter answers itself.

concepts.name: board
concepts.definition: One ranking of the leaderboard for one period, as one viewer sees it: the Everyone board ranks members across the workspace by kudos given, the My group board the members of the viewer's primary group, and the Groups board the groups by kudos given per member. Its rows are cut to the window.

concepts.name: window
concepts.definition: The rows a board shows one viewer: positions 1-3, then the viewer's position with up to three above and three below, or the first ten positions when the viewer is 7th or better, never more than ten rows, with one gap line where positions are skipped; a viewer who gave nothing sees positions 1-3 and how to join (G17).

concepts.name: improvement line
concepts.definition: The one private line under a viewer's Everyone board for this week or month: how many more kudos they gave than in the previous period up to the same day, with the places climbed, or else their best completed period; it never states a loss, and all time has none (G18).

concepts.name: app home tab
concepts.definition: One page of App Home, picked from the tab bar at its top, each shown only while its own flag is on: Profile (the member's kudos and allowance, and their level while xp-levels is on), Leaderboard (the boards for one period, while everyone-board is on), Settings (the member's own switches of the flags that are on) and Admin (the announcement channel, for workspace admins and owners while xp-levels is on); with both flags off App Home has no tab bar. App Home remembers the tab and period each member last picked, and opens a remembered tab whose flag is off on Profile (G24, G42).

concepts.name: product event
concepts.definition: A fact of the domain sent to PostHog under a name from the lexicon, written <object> <past-tense verb> in lowercase words (kudos given, kudos received), with only the properties its projection lists by name. Not a domain event: a domain event drives the domain, a product event only reports it.

concepts.name: analytics ID
concepts.definition: A member's opaque identity in PostHog: a random UUID the analytics module creates the first time it records a product event for the member or a mutation reads a flag for them, and keeps while the member's data exists. Sent as distinct_id; never derived from a Slack ID, a name, an email or a Convex document ID, and sent together with the member's profile (email, names, title, Slack user and team ID) only in person events.

concepts.name: workspace key
concepts.definition: A workspace's opaque identity in PostHog: a random UUID the analytics module creates the first time it records a product event for the workspace, sent as workspace_key on every product event. Never the Slack team ID.

concepts.name: outbox
concepts.definition: The analytics module's table of product events recorded and not yet delivered to PostHog. An event is written there in the transaction that makes its fact true, or in the subscriber transaction its domain event schedules, and leaves it when PostHog accepts its batch.

concepts.name: drain
concepts.definition: The one analytics action that sends the outbox's due product events to PostHog's batch endpoint, at most 100 per request, and settles each batch by PostHog's answer. Only one drain runs at a time; recording starts it when none is scheduled or running.

concepts.name: capture
concepts.definition: Whether a deployment records and sends product events: on only when it has both the PostHog project token and a valid KUDOS_ENVIRONMENT (sandbox or production). With capture off nothing is recorded and nothing is sent.

concepts.name: exhausted
concepts.definition: An outbox event the drain has given up and will never send: rejected by PostHog (400 or 413), out of retries after its sixth failure, or expired after 7 days pending. It is logged once with its name and reason, never its properties, and deleted 7 days later. Its reason exhausted names the second case.

concepts.name: usage fact
concepts.definition: A platform-neutral fact a chat adapter reports to the analytics module when a member uses the app outside a kudos message: App Home opened, or a command typed with its result. It is recorded in the mutation that handles it and becomes a product event; it drives nothing in the domain.

concepts.name: error boundary
concepts.definition: The wrapper every HTTP route and action outside the analytics module runs inside. When the function throws an error nobody caught, it records one exception for PostHog Error Tracking in its own transaction and rethrows an error marked [reported], so Convex and Slack still see the failure and no outer boundary or the failed-job sweep reports it again. If recording fails, it logs a fixed code and rethrows the original error.

concepts.name: reportable error
concepts.definition: An error this codebase throws on purpose with a message written only from fixed text and Slack error codes, such as a Slack call that answered not_authed. It is the only error whose message is sent to PostHog; every other error is sent as unexpected error with its type name.

concepts.name: failed-job sweep
concepts.definition: The analytics mutation a cron runs every 15 minutes that finds scheduled functions which failed without an error boundary reporting them, and records each once as an exception. It pages through new scheduled functions from a cursor, keeps every unfinished one on a watch list until it finishes, and never reports the analytics module's own functions.

concepts.name: flag
concepts.definition: A switch declared once in code with its key, its values and a safe default, and no fixed subject; PostHog decides it twice, as a member decision and as a workspace decision; a new member-facing slice ships behind one whose safe default is off

concepts.name: exposure
concepts.definition: The $feature_flag_called event sent once per member, flag and value, from the mutation in which the member first enters the flagged path

concepts.name: moment
concepts.definition: A full-screen celebration on the website of one thing that happened to the member: a level up, an achievement, kudos received, a new hedgehog, or a crate opened. It plays in full the first time it is seen, then opens on its end state with a replay.

concepts.name: crate
concepts.definition: How a member takes something the game has ready for them: a feature their level made ready, or a finished quest or Journey step. Opening it is one action: a feature's crate and a quest's crate whose reward counted at its finish only reveal what is already recorded, a quest's crate holding a held reward applies that reward once, at its first open, and a crate a member opens themselves can drop a hoggie nobody knows before the open. What it records is known before it opens; its hoggie is not.

concepts.name: medal
concepts.definition: How the website draws an achievement's tier: a neutral metal rosette (bronze, silver, gold or diamond) with one to four pips and the tier's word beside it. A medal is never a rarity colour.

concepts.name: team
concepts.definition: A team on the company's website, such as posthog.com/teams/workflows, with its crest and team photo. A group maps to at most one team by name, and the website shows the team's crest and photo for it. Kudos never count for a team: they count for groups.

concepts.name: company profile
concepts.definition: A person's public profile on the company's website, with their photo and colour. The website shows a member by their company profile when the member's Slack name matches exactly one, and otherwise falls back to the Slack photo, then initials.

concepts.name: Quill
concepts.definition: PostHog's design system (@posthog/quill): the components and colour tokens the website is built from (ADR-0005). The website's colours come only from its tokens, apart from the moment bands, the medal metals and a company profile's colour behind that person's face.

concepts.name: ship sweep
concepts.definition: Unlocks' hourly scheduled mutation that turns a feature's flag turning on into readiness: it stores readiness, publishes unlockReady and sends one DM per member for every member at or past the level of a shipped feature who has none stored (P78).

concepts.name: ready pill
concepts.definition: The button in the website's HUD that counts the crates ready for the signed-in member, as "{n} ready", and opens the first through the same command as the crate's Open. It is gone at zero, and something that becomes ready during a visit joins it instead of opening by itself (V1, V15, WS68).

concepts.name: quest
concepts.definition: A goal a member pursues for a reward: one of the 3 personal quests drawn for their week, the group quest, or a step of the Journey. Finishing it records its reward at once in a reward record; its crate only reveals it. A quest counts only once its feature is open, because quests are goals, not earnings.

concepts.name: Journey
concepts.definition: The fixed chain of onboarding steps, each keyed by a stable step ID such as first-thanks, never by its number. Its first step is active from the start, every other step when its feature is opened; a step's reward is fixed when it becomes active, and finishing records exactly that. Steps never expire, restart, block a level or count toward the weekly quests.

concepts.name: reward record
concepts.definition: One insert-only record of what finishing a quest or Journey step pays: its XP, coins, item and catalogue version, fixed when the quest was drawn or the step became active. It is keyed by what it pays for (a Journey step: member and step); progression writes it once. One written without held counts toward XP, levels and the wallet at its finish, like effects records; a held reward counts only from its crate's first open (CR1-CR4).

concepts.name: quest pool
concepts.definition: The versioned catalogue of personal quests a weekly draw picks from: each quest has a stable ID, a kind (breadth, thoughtfulness or participation), its goal copy, its progress predicate over what the member gives, its needs and its reward. It holds only quests whose needs have shipped, and always at least 3 a member can finish alone on the last day of a week.

concepts.name: swap
concepts.definition: A member's once-a-week replacement of one unfinished weekly quest with a feasible quest not in that week's draw, stored for good with the replaced quest, the new quest and the facts that made it feasible (P81, the spec's reroll).

concepts.name: Book
concepts.definition: The feature that opens at level 4, where a member sees their achievement ladders and the tiers they earned, each with its date; it opens achievements, and the sticker book with its albums once that ships.

concepts.name: qualifying recognition
concepts.definition: The first award from a giver to a recipient on the giver's day whose stored gate decision says it is thoughtful kudos, from a kudos message or, later, a chime-in. Every per-recognition bonus XP line and giving coin pays once per qualifying recognition, however many kudos the award carries; base XP still counts every kudos. Whether an award is one, and whether it is the giver's first of the day or the first to that recipient in the giver's week, is kept for every award whether or not the giver owns a perk (P16, P17).

concepts.name: launch batch
concepts.definition: The ladders and tiers one mutation finds unevaluated in a workspace, the Book's launch or the first mutation after a deploy that adds one, replayed together: every tier their replays earn carries the batch, and the batch is complete only when all its replays are (P62).

concepts.name: applause
concepts.definition: The ladder that counts the days a member thanked 3 or more different people, on the giver's day, across any number of messages that day (P58, P59).

concepts.name: seasons
concepts.definition: The ladder that counts the calendar months in which a member gave a kudos, on the giver's day (P58, P59).

concepts.name: connections
concepts.definition: The ladder that counts the different people a member has thanked (P58).

concepts.name: dependability
concepts.definition: The ladder that counts the days on which a member gave a kudos, on the giver's day; a day counts once (P58, P59).

concepts.name: Old Friends
concepts.definition: The ladder that counts the times a member thanked someone again 30 or more of the giver's days after the giver's previous award to them; a first thanks to someone counts nothing (P58).

concepts.name: reward
concepts.definition: What a goal or a tier promises a member, fixed when it is promised: a quest's or Journey step's XP, coins and item, paid once through a reward record (P86, P87), or a tier's reward kind and reward ID, paid once that kind ships (P58, P62)

concepts.name: gains line
concepts.definition: The parts of a Given success reply's extras line that say what the kudos earned its giver, in one order joined with ' · ': the base XP the whole message gave them (+{xp} XP, from Progression's one function the effects records use), each quest it finished with its own reward (Quest done: {goal} (+{xp} XP)), and the bonus each owned perk paid on it, summed over the message's awards ({perk} bonus (+{xp} XP)); stored as facts when the reply is written and shown at each delivery only as far as the giver can still see them, the bonus parts only while the skill tree applies (SW1-SW5, amending P71). The activity's given entries follow its parts and its view rule.

concepts.name: route list
concepts.definition: The website pages Slack may link to, each as SITE_URL plus its route: exactly the paths the website's router serves, kept equal to the router's own list by a contract test (SW9, SW10). A page that isn't listed yet resolves to Home.

concepts.name: deep link
concepts.definition: A link at the end of a Slack message to one member that opens the listed website page its subject lives on, built by the website's one link function and shown only while that function answers one, so never in a public message (SW11, SW13, SW14, SW16).

concepts.name: front door
concepts.definition: App Home for a member to whom the website's link function answers a Home link (the website flag on, SITE_URL set, the deployment's workspace): a Profile summary of the allowance, one level line, the crates waiting with Open, the week's quests with Swap and a row of buttons to Home and each open feature with a listed page, beside Settings and Admin as before; a tab whose feature has a listed page gives way to its button (SW19 to SW24).

concepts.name: member decision
concepts.definition: A flag's answer for one member: evaluated on the member's analytics ID with the person properties environment and, when the directory holds one, email; in a query, for a member without an analytics ID, it is the workspace decision. It decides everything that one member sees, gets or does

concepts.name: workspace decision
concepts.definition: A flag's answer for the workspace: evaluated on the workspace key with the person property environment only, so an email condition never matches it. It decides only what the workspace shares: what a channel shows, what a person the directory doesn't know sees, and the moments that happen once for the whole workspace

concepts.name: preview
concepts.definition: A member's state for one flag while their member decision is on and the workspace decision is off, through a release condition on their email: they see and get the feature alone, nothing of it shows in a channel or a shared setting, and ending it takes nothing away (F16-F25)

concepts.name: user group
concepts.definition: A Slack user group as the directory keeps it: its handle, its name, whether it is enabled or one of Slack's automatic admin and owner groups, and the people in it, refreshed from Slack whenever Slack says it changed and once a day. A group is a user group that counts for Kudos. A workspace on a Slack plan without user groups has none.

concepts.name: job
concepts.definition: A function Convex runs later from its scheduler: a scheduled mutation or action, such as a retry, a bus subscriber, a members list or a continuation of a batch. One call may schedule at most 1,000 jobs, and a job that fails without an error boundary reporting it is what the failed-job sweep finds.

concepts.name: analytics
concepts.definition: The only module that knows PostHog: it projects domain events and the chat adapter's usage facts into product events, records them and exceptions in its outbox while capture is on, drains them to PostHog, evaluates flags with their exposures, and keeps each member's analytics ID and each workspace's workspace key. It observes and never changes what a member sees.

concepts.name: preview moment
concepts.definition: The once-per-member moment a preview gets in place of a workspace moment: the first mutation that shows a feature to a member whose workspace has no launch of it stores it once and, for unlocks, opens for that member alone every feature shipped in their member decision then, at that moment and without a DM, and for quests joins that member alone to the Journey as of that moment, as the Journey's join joins a member who existed at its ship moment (F22); the workspace moment later adds only what that member is missing (F23)

concepts.name: person event
concepts.definition: A PostHog $identify or $set the analytics module records for one analytics ID, carrying the member's profile as person properties ($set, and $unset of what the profile lost) beside O2's properties; the only kind of event that carries a profile, and so names, emails or Slack IDs.

concepts.name: bonus
concepts.definition: Bonus XP: XP a recognition earns beyond base XP, apart from quest and Journey rewards. While the skill tree applies, each effect perk the giver owns that pays on a qualifying recognition writes one bonus line { source, xp } on the giver's effects record, fixed when the record is written and never recomputed (ADR-0004). A Given reply separately stores, when it is written, each perk's bonus summed over the message's awards, and while the skill tree still applies at delivery the gains line shows each as '{perk} bonus (+{xp} XP)' after base XP and any Quest done parts; that stored amount can differ from effects records written later. Later, reaching a chime-in threshold gives its recipients bonus XP. Not the perk, which pays it, and not the gains line, which shows it; the weekly reserve's bonus kudos and the bonus quest are other things.

concepts.name: places climbed
concepts.definition: How many positions a ranked row of a board rose against the same board in the previous period up to the same day (G18's comparison): a positive number, or nothing when it didn't rise, wasn't on that board then, or the period is all time; no read ever states a drop, and Slack shows none (GB18). The improvement line's places are the viewer's own.

concepts.name: admin
concepts.definition: A workspace admin or owner in Slack, read from the directory (GB26, P69). Only admins see the Admin tab, and an admin command (setAnnouncementChannel, setGroupMode) from anyone else changes nothing.

concepts.name: group mode
concepts.definition: Which user groups count as groups in a workspace (GB27): every group, the default, or allowlist mode, where only the groups on the allowlist count. An admin sets it with setGroupMode in the Admin tab; it takes effect at that instant and reconciles every member's primary group.

concepts.name: allowlist
concepts.definition: The groups an admin picked in allowlist mode of the group mode (GB1, GB27): only they count. It is kept when the mode goes back to every group, so switching back restores it, and an empty one makes groups unavailable (GB3).

concepts.name: attribution
concepts.definition: The record that a Given kudos message counts for the giver's primary group at its spend instant, or for no group: made once per message after reconciling the giver, insert-only, with its kudos, allowance day, spend instant, each award's stored gate decision and each recipient's primary group at that instant, and published as awardsAttributed (GB10). Group totals and the group quest follow it, never kudosGiven itself. Not Coherence's attribution of a journal record to its session and agent.

concepts.name: group total
concepts.definition: The kudos one member gave for one group in one period (week, month or all time), with the period's running total by day for a week or month, fed only by awardsAttributed, exactly once per kudos message (GB12, GB30). A cache: it can be rebuilt from the attributions.

concepts.name: group board
concepts.definition: One of the boards above the Everyone board where groups apply to the viewer and groups are available: the Groups board, which ranks every group that is the current primary group of at least 3 members by the kudos attributed to it in the period per current primary member, then participation, total and name, with the viewer's group's line and the most improved group; and the My group board, which ranks the members of the viewer's primary group by the kudos they gave for it (GB13–GB17).

concepts.name: peer line
concepts.definition: The private line right after the Everyone board's improvement line, for this week and this month, telling a viewer whose gain is above 0 and larger than more than half of the other current primary members of their group (at least 3 of them) that they improved more than a share of it, rounded down to a multiple of 10 (GB16).

concepts.name: wallet
concepts.definition: A member's coins: the coins on their effects and reward records minus what they spent, kept as a cached balance that never goes below 0, never expires and can't be moved to anyone else (CO9-CO12, ADR-0003). Only the wallet module writes the balance and the insert-only spend records.

concepts.name: upgrade
concepts.definition: A perk that replaces a perk the member owns with a stronger line, costing skill points and coins: it requires the perk it upgrades, and once owned its line is paid instead of its base's.

concepts.name: category
concepts.definition: One of the Book's four groups of achievement ladders (Giving, Being thanked, Connections, Crowd), each with its own page, name, blurb and hedgehog emblem; the website keys every ladder to one.

concepts.name: kudos text
concepts.definition: The stored words of a kudos message's newest revision: its text as segments in order, its channel's visibility, its author and that revision's gate decision. It is the only message text the app stores, kept while the message is a kudos message and replaced by a word-free tombstone when the message is edited away or deleted.

concepts.name: activity
concepts.definition: A member's own timeline of the kudos they received and gave, newest first, with each kudos's words and Slack permalink, read only by that member on the website behind the activity flag.

concepts.name: permalink
concepts.definition: Slack's link to one message, built from the workspace's URL, the channel and the message's ts, with the thread root for a thread reply, never from a Slack call per message.

concepts.name: spotlight
concepts.definition: One drawable kudos shown on the leaderboard page with its words, giver, recipients and Slack permalink: a Given kudos from a public channel whose current words said why, by a member, with nobody on it off the leaderboards; drawn at random from the member's own workspace, and Next walks every drawable kudos once before any repeat.

concepts.name: held reward
concepts.definition: A reward record for a weekly quest or Journey step written while crate-rewards was on for its member, marked held at insert. It counts toward nothing (no XP, level, skill point or coin) until its crate's first open applies it, once, from Slack or the website; achievement tier coins are never held, and the record, not the flag, decides.

concepts.name: item
concepts.definition: A kudos emoji or hedgehog a member can own, with a stable ID, a name, its art and exactly one source: the starter, the store or an achievement tier.

concepts.name: inventory
concepts.definition: A member's loadout and collection together, opened with Coins.

concepts.name: message setting
concepts.definition: A member's choice, one place per kind of message HedgeHug sends them (the after-kudos reply, tips, level ups, new features, quests and the Journey, Book tiers and public celebrations): in the channel (an ephemeral only they see, beside the kudos message that caused it), as a DM, or none, among the places the kind allows. Every kind arrives where it arrives today until the member changes it; the earlier App Home switches that turned DMs off or muted public notices read as those kinds none. A message of a kind set to none is not written and not sent when Slack takes it; one with no kudos message behind it, or that Slack refuses beside it, arrives as a DM. Errors that need action, the welcome message, the answer to a Buy, App Home and a /hedgehug reply are never turned off.

concepts.name: custom emoji
concepts.definition: An emoji a workspace added to Slack beyond the standard set, kept in the directory by name with its https image (an alias with its original's image), so the website can show it where a kudos's words name it.

concepts.name: Buy
concepts.definition: The button on a perk offer, in App Home's Skill tree tab, in a level-up message and on the website, that buys the perk for the member who clicks it; its answer, what they bought or why not, reaches only that member (QM26).

concepts.name: hoggie
concepts.definition: An official PostHog hedgehog illustration from @posthog/brand, named by its slug, that a member collects in the Book: every crate a member opens drops one, drawn by its rarity at the open, and duplicates count up. A hoggie is not an item: it fills no slot, is never sold and is never a kudos emoji.

concepts.name: crest
concepts.definition: A team's crest from @posthog/brand, named by its slug, that a member collects in the Book once they hold at least one of every hoggie on its roster of two to four hoggies; it is collected once, at the drop that completed the roster, and never taken back. It is the art of a team, not a group.

concepts.name: group quest
concepts.definition: A group's one shared quest for a group week (Monday 00:00 UTC to the next): drawn from its participants at the week's start, with a target of min(3, participants - 1) contributors; every contributor gets its reward once the target is reached. It shows counts, never names (GB21-GB24, P82).

concepts.name: contribution
concepts.definition: A participant's part in their group quest: recorded once per participant, group and group week, at their first award attributed to the group and spent in that week that does the quest's action (GB22, GB30).

concepts.name: Monday post
concepts.definition: The weekly public post in the announcement channel that celebrates last week's top groups (GB28): up to three groups with their kudos per person, the most improved group and how many people gave kudos, never naming a member. An admin switches it on with setMondayPost in the Admin tab; it goes out every Monday at 9:00 in the admin's time zone, at most once per week, and not in a week nobody gave.

concepts.name: roster
concepts.definition: A crest's frozen list of two to four hoggies; a member who holds at least one of each has collected the crest. Every catalogue version 1 hoggie is on exactly one roster, and a published roster never changes.

retired.name: DM setting
retired.definition: App Home's earlier switch over progression DMs (P63), now read and written through the member's message setting: it shows on while any of the four DM kinds (level ups, new features, quests and the Journey, Book tiers) is on, and sets all four. A stored DM setting off reads as those kinds off. It never silences the welcome message, and changes no XP or level.
retired.because: decision 24 (#376): one message setting per kind replaces the DM setting; the product owner's words retire it

rejected.because: decision 24 (#376): one message setting per kind replaces the DM setting; the product owner's words retire it
